identity.title: Jolt accentuation of headache (2-3 Hz horizontal head rotation)

technique.how: Ask the patient with a current headache to rotate the head horizontally ('no-no') 2-3 times per second for a few seconds, or rotate it passively. Positive if the baseline headache is clearly worsened by the movement.
technique.prerequisites: Patient must have a headache and be alert enough to report change; intended for febrile patients with recent-onset headache and normal mental status.
technique.contraindications: Cervical spine injury; severe vertebrobasilar disease is a relative caution.

interpretation.positive_finding: In the original selected cohort (fever, recent headache, no altered mental status) a positive jolt sign had sensitivity 0.97 for CSF pleocytosis; pooled data give sensitivity ~0.65 and specificity ~0.70, so a positive result modestly supports LP.
interpretation.negative_finding: A negative jolt sign does not exclude meningitis: pooled sensitivity 0.65 (0.75 in alert patients) and only 0.21 in an ED cohort; sensitivity was near 1.0 only in the narrow original population.
interpretation.pitfalls: Cannot be used without headache or in altered mental status, where meningitis risk is highest. Unselected populations include non-meningitic causes of pleocytosis, which lowers apparent accuracy.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: obtain CSF even without neck stiffness; negative: still LP if altered mental status, focal deficit, immunocompromise or high pretest probability.

estimates.target_condition: Acute meningitis (CSF pleocytosis) in suspected meningitis
estimates.population: Adults and adolescents with suspected meningitis; 9 cross-sectional studies (1161 participants)
estimates.reference_standard: CSF pleocytosis (8 studies) or pleocytosis plus raised CSF protein; culture/smear in 2
estimates.quote: Overall, pooled sensitivity was 65.3% (95% confidence interval (CI) 37.3 to 85.6), and pooled specificity was 70.4% (95% CI 47.7 to 86.1)

estimates.target_condition: Acute meningitis (CSF pleocytosis), participants with undisturbed consciousness
estimates.population: Subgroup with undisturbed consciousness; 8 studies, 921 participants
estimates.quote: pooled sensitivity and specificity were 75.2% (95% CI 54.3 to 88.6) and 60.8% (95% CI 43.4 to 75.9), respectively

estimates.population: 54 febrile patients with recent-onset headache undergoing LP on suspicion of meningitis, Japan (original description)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.971/(1-0.60); LR- = (1-0.971)/0.60; from 33/34 with pleocytosis positive and 12/20 without pleocytosis negative (abstract); prevalence 34/54
estimates.quote: Among 34 patients with pleocytosis, 33 had jolt accentuation (sensitivity: 97.1%) ... Among 20 patients without pleocytosis, 12 had no jolt accentuation (specificity: 60%)

estimates.target_condition: Meningitis among patients with fever and headache (RCE recalculation of the 1991 cohort)
estimates.quote: sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 54%, positive likelihood ratio of 2.2, and negative likelihood ratio of 0

estimates.population: 197 neurologically intact ED adults with headache undergoing LP, altered mental status excluded; 2 inner-city academic EDs
estimates.reference_standard: CSF pleocytosis >=5 cells/high-power field in 4th tube
estimates.quote: For pleocytosis, the sensitivity of jolt accentuation was 21% ... The specificity of jolt accentuation was 82%

estimates.population: 8 case-control datasets, adults with suspected meningitis, mostly Japan/Iran

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Not applicable without headache, in altered mental status, focal deficits, or possible cervical spine injury; never use a negative test alone to omit LP in high-risk patients.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Altered mental status or neurological deficit indicates intracranial pathology needing imaging/LP and empiric therapy regardless of jolt result.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Akaishi 2019 describes the maneuver as more consistent between examiners than nuchal rigidity, but no kappa was available in the sources seen.

extraction_notes: Primary pooled estimate is the Cochrane 2020 bivariate model (abstract; very low certainty, high heterogeneity). Uchihara 1991 LRs are computed from abstract counts. Attia 1999 abstract reports sensitivity 100%/LR- 0 for the same cohort (their recalculation differs from Uchihara's 97.1%); entered separately, not averaged. Akaishi 2019 Table 2 from PMC full text uses 99% CIs and simple summation. Tamune 2019 is a systematic review without pooling (cited for population-selection interpretation only, kind set to meta_analysis as closest schema option). Nakao and Uchihara quotes join two abstract fragments with an ellipsis.
